To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dynamic redistribution of subcellular stored total calcium in the spindle and the pericentriole regions of the cytoplasm is a key component of the time-dependent preparation of mammalian LLC-Pk1 cells for mitosis and cytokinesis.

1) the total calcium concentration is highest in the spindle region and lowest in the central region of a metaphase spindle in a single mammalian cell and 2) the dynamic alignment of calcium in both half-spindle regions may be an integral process in the preparation of a cell to exit the metaphase stage.

SIMS ion microscopy is a powerful technique for the quantitative 3-D analysis of the distribution of total cellular calcium stores in subcellular organelles of living mammalian cells undergoing mitosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for quantitative 3-D subcellular imaging of stored calcium in mammalian cells by SIMS ion microscope.
developing and applying a new methodology for quantitatively mapping total calcium in subcellular organelles and cytoplasmic regions in individual mammalian cells in the context of mitosis.
the development and application of SIMS ion microscopy to the study of the distribution and dynamics of total cellular and subcellular calcium in living cells and tissues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the redistribution of the intercellular calcium store in the mitotic cells was not due to a simple redistribution of the interphasic Golgi calcium store, but to a more complex process of calcium store redistribution in both the spindle region and the non-spindly cytoplasm.
calcium is involved in mitosis and the dynamic alignment of calcium is a prerequisite for the onset of an anaphase.
SIMS imaging of subcellulat calcium stores is an important new tool for the investigation of calcium dynamics in the living cell and in particular for the investigation of the mitotic spindle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the total calcium gradients in the cytoplasm of mitotic cells are dynamic, and they are correlated to the cell cycle stages and to the subcellular calcium storage compartments in mammalian epithelial cells.

the total calcium gradients measured with SIMS ion microscopy in the spindle and non-spindle regions of mammalian cells are consistent with the presence of both IP3-sensitive calcium stores and calcium stores sensitive to thapsigargin.
SIMS ion microscopy provides a powerful and unique approach to study the dynamic redistribution of subcellular stores of total calcium in mammalian cells undergoing mitosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamic alignment of calcium in the mitotic spindle may play a role in the regulation of mitosis in mammalian LLC cells.
the total calcium concentrations in subcellular compartments are not constant during cell division, but vary dynamically in the interphase and mitotic cells.

SIMS ion microscopy is a powerful quantitative technique for the study of the dynamic distribution of subcellular stored Ca2+ and other elements in cells and organelles undergoing mitosis and meiosis.
